title_en: The $7 Trillion Market Most Advisors Can't Actually Access | Chris Getter, Simplify
title_zh: 大多数顾问其实碰不到的 7 万亿美元市场 | Chris Getter，Simplify
subtitle_zh: Simplify 董事总经理兼基金经理 Chris Getter 拆解 FOXY：如何把机构级的货币套息交易装进一只 ETF，为越来越失效的 60/40 组合提供一个真正低相关的另类收益来源
description: The $7 Trillion Market Most Advisors Can't Actually Access | Chris Getter, Simplify

turns.en: Welcome to Behind the Ticker, the podcast where we go beyond the symbol and into the strategy. I'm Brad Roth, founder and chief investment officer at Thor Funds, and in each episode I sit down with ETF managers, CIOs, and industry leaders to break down how these funds are
turns.zh: 欢迎收听 Behind the Ticker，一档带你越过代码、深入策略的播客。我是 Brad Roth，Thor Funds 的创始人兼首席投资官。每一期节目，我都会和 ETF 基金经理、首席投资官以及行业领袖坐下来，拆解这些基金到底是

turns.en: actually built, how they behave in real markets, and how advisors use them in real portfolios. Most people will just see a ticker symbol, but we know much more goes on behind the ticker.
turns.zh: 怎么构建出来的、在真实市场里表现如何，以及投资顾问在真实组合里是怎么用它们的。大多数人看到的只是一个股票代码，但我们知道，代码背后还有多得多的东西。

turns.en: Hey Chris, welcome to the show. Thanks for having me Brad, glad to be here. So why don't we start by you giving everybody a bit about your background. I saw you spend about a decade in currency and emerging markets trading before joining Simplify as a managing director and portfolio manager.
turns.zh: 嗨 Chris，欢迎来到节目。谢谢邀请，Brad，很高兴能来。那不如先从你给大家讲讲自己的背景开始吧。我注意到，在加入 Simplify 出任董事总经理兼基金经理之前，你在货币和新兴市场交易这一行做了差不多十年。

turns.en: So can you kind of walk us through higher career unfolded? Yeah, I started actually started in US high yield.
turns.zh: 那你能给我们讲讲，你的职业道路是怎么一步步走过来的吗？好的，其实我最早是从美国高收益债（US high yield）开始的。

turns.en: At fidelity investments back in the mid 1990s, that was about the time that emerging markets was starting to unravel right after the Mexican peso crisis, kind of the middle of the Asia currency crisis and then before Russia defaulted. And it looked like those guys who we sat next to were having a lot more fun.
turns.zh: 那是在 Fidelity Investments，1990 年代中期。那个时候新兴市场（emerging markets）正好开始崩盘：墨西哥比索危机刚过去，正处在亚洲货币危机的中途，然后俄罗斯又违约了。而坐在我们旁边的那帮人，看起来玩得开心多了。

turns.en: So I did my best to transition to that team and I've never looked back. I've spent substantially all of my career in EM either doing sovereigns, currencies, local rates, a little bit of corporates. I went to PIMCO in 2008, spent about 10 years there and then spent 10 minutes at Lesard asset management also in EM.
turns.zh: 所以我就想方设法转到了那个团队，从此再没回头。我的职业生涯基本上全都花在新兴市场（EM）上，做过主权债、货币、本地利率，也做过一点公司债。2008 年我去了 PIMCO，在那儿待了大约十年，然后在 Lazard Asset Management 待了十分钟，同样是做新兴市场。

turns.en: Then I thought it was retired and then low and behold, I'm back here at Simplify doing what I've done before. In large part. So I always ask people before we get into the nuts and bolts, what do they like to do for fun? But I see the guitars behind you. I'm assuming you like to play the guitar.
turns.zh: 然后我以为自己退休了，结果你猜怎么着，我又回到了 Simplify，在很大程度上干着我以前干过的那套活儿。那在我们进入具体细节之前，我总会先问嘉宾一个问题：平时喜欢做点什么消遣？我看到你身后摆着吉他，我猜你喜欢弹吉他。

turns.en: I do like to play it. I will break it out and the only thing that we'll do is ensure that I'm never invited back to your podcast. That's okay. So anyways, let's talk about Simplify. The firm was founded in 2020 by David Burns has built a reputation for bringing institutional
turns.zh: 我确实喜欢弹。我要是把它拿出来，唯一的效果就是确保你再也不会请我上你的播客了。那没关系。好了，我们还是来聊聊 Simplify 吧。这家公司由 David Burns 在 2020 年创立，已经在把机构级

turns.en: grade strategies, alternatives, income, all of these things in ETF wrapper. So before we get into Foxy, which is what we're here to talk about. Can you talk about Simplify as a whole and the firm? Sure. So I'll add a name to that list. It was Dave Burns and Paul Kim, somebody who I worked with closely at PIMCO for a number of years.
turns.zh: 策略、另类资产（alternatives）、收益型产品，所有这些东西装进 ETF 这个外壳里这件事上打出了名气。那在我们进入今天的主角 FOXY 之前，你能先整体介绍一下 Simplify 这家公司吗？当然。那我要往那份名单上再加一个名字：是 Dave Burns 和 Paul Kim，Paul 是我在 PIMCO 共事过很多年的同事。

turns.en: They started it in 2020 and it was really what I think of as is almost a recognition of a structural break in what ETFs could do for the individual investor. In 2019, the SEC promulgated an update or a refresh to how ETFs were regulated, what they could hold, how they would be risk-managed and evaluated by the SEC.
turns.zh: 他们 2020 年创办了这家公司。在我看来，这几乎就是源于一种认知：ETF 能为个人投资者做的事情，出现了一次结构性的断裂。2019 年，SEC 发布了一项更新，也可以说是对 ETF 监管方式的一次刷新——ETF 可以持有什么、如何进行风险管理、SEC 会怎么评估它们。

turns.en: And that really opened the floodgates for basically you could do anything in an ETF that you could do in a traditional mutual fund structure, derivatives, convex strategies, all sorts of things that previously didn't really lend themselves to being packaged in an ETF format.
turns.zh: 这基本上打开了闸门：过去你在传统共同基金结构里能做的事，现在都能在 ETF 里做了——衍生品、凸性策略（convex strategies），以及各种以前其实并不适合装进 ETF 这种形式里的东西。

turns.en: And it comes with all the benefits of being an ETF, daily liquidity, transparency, the tax advantage for clients that that matters for. And so that recognition I think was the genesis of Simplify to say like, hey, we can do this and we can bring something that's extraordinarily
turns.zh: 而且还附带 ETF 本身的全部好处：每日流动性、透明度，以及对那些在意税务的客户来说的税务优势。所以我认为，正是这种认知成了 Simplify 的起点——就是说，嘿，我们能做这件事，我们能把一些极其

turns.en: beneficial that has traditionally been solely the domain of institutional clients. So let's get right into Foxy FOX-Y. It's the Simplify currency strategy ETF. You guys launched this in 2025. Looks like in February of 2025, actively managed at a high level,
turns.zh: 有益、而过去一直只属于机构客户专属领域的东西带给大家。那我们就直接进入 FOXY 吧。它是 Simplify Currency Strategy ETF，你们在 2025 年发行了这只基金，看起来是 2025 年 2 月，属于主动管理（actively managed）。从大的层面上讲，

turns.en: what's the fund and what's the problem in solving? Sure. So the problem it is solving is to generate absolute return that does not behave or is not delivered in a pattern that matches what you get from equities or what you get from bonds. So you get the return and you get the
turns.zh: 这只基金到底是什么，它要解决的问题是什么？好。它要解决的问题，是提供一种绝对收益（absolute return），而且这种收益的表现方式、兑现路径，都不跟你从股票里拿到的、或者从债券里拿到的那种模式重合。所以你既拿到了收益，又拿到了

turns.en: diversification benefit. When we think of how portfolios are increasingly being constructed by advisors, you've got the old 6040, that's now migrating to something like 50, 30, 20 or perhaps that 20 might be larger. And it's not an alternative bucket where you hold one thing.
turns.zh: 分散化（diversification）的好处。想想投资顾问们现在越来越多地是怎么构建组合的：老式的 60/40 正在迁移到类似 50/30/20 这样的结构，或者那个 20 的比例可能更大。而这个另类桶，不该是一个只装着一样东西的桶。

turns.en: It should be an alternative bucket. You want to diversify that the same way that you wouldn't put your 60 in one stock. You should hold many alternatives. And Foxy fits pretty squarely into that in terms of getting you the low correlation, the diversification benefit against stocks and
turns.zh: 它应该是一个另类桶，你要对它做分散配置，就像你不会把那 60% 的部分全押在一只股票上一样。你应该持有很多种另类资产。而 FOXY 正好严丝合缝地落在这个定位里：它给你低相关性，给你相对于股票和

turns.en: bonds. But it also diversifies nicely against other things that are traditionally conceived of as alternatives. Interesting. So the FX market is the largest, most liquid market in the world. Most retail investors just don't understand it. Never really, and they have access to the currency
turns.zh: 债券的分散化好处。但它相对于其他那些传统上被视作另类资产的东西，也能很好地起到分散作用。有意思。外汇（FX）市场是全球规模最大、流动性最强的市场。大多数散户投资者根本不了解它，其实他们也一直没有真正接触过货币

turns.en: market as an asset class. But it seems a little bit scary when you try to access it. So can you walk us through why that's been such a persistent gap and what Foxy's actually bringing to the table? Yeah, it's it's funny, Brett, I had watched before I came on or the past couple of weeks,
turns.zh: 市场，把它当成一个资产类别。但当你真要去接触它的时候，它又显得有点吓人。那你能给我们讲讲，为什么这个缺口一直存在，FOXY 到底带来了什么？有意思的是，Brad，在我上节目之前的这几周里，

turns.en: I've watched a lot of your podcasts. This is the one strategy where you can't go to your brokerage account and say, I want to buy something that's in the fun. The for the currency market is primarily transacted with instruments that are called forward contracts. There are a lot like futures.
turns.zh: 我看了你不少期播客。货币是唯一一种策略，你没法打开自己的券商账户然后说“我想买这只基金里的某个东西”。因为货币市场主要是用一种叫做远期合约（forward contracts）的工具来交易的。它们在很多方面很像期货。

turns.en: But it's nothing you would go to your brokerage platform and be able to find and say, I want that in my portfolio, answering your question of why it has traditionally been so mystical to investors. I think there's a couple of reasons. One is it always comes packaged with something else.
turns.zh: 但你没法在券商平台上找到它，然后说“我想把这个放进我的组合里”。这也回答了你的问题：为什么它对投资者来说一直这么神秘。我觉得有几个原因。第一，它总是跟别的东西打包在一起出现。

turns.en: If you buy European stocks, you are naturally exposing yourself to the euro. Maybe you do it hazed or unhaged, but you probably don't give it any thought that you now have a euro-denominated investment in the same holds true in the global bond market. That's number one. Number two,
turns.zh: 如果你买欧洲股票，你就自然而然地暴露在了欧元之下。也许你会做对冲（hedged）或者不做对冲，但你大概根本不会想到，自己现在持有了一笔以欧元计价的投资；同样的道理在全球债券市场上也成立。这是第一点。第二点，

turns.en: this is a more practical thing. Most currencies trade inverse. So if the Mexican peso goes from 17 to 18 and you're a long peso, you've lost money, right? The peso weakened and now it buys, when you convert it back, it buys fewer dollars. I think there's a little bit of, you know, maybe
turns.zh: 这一点更实际一些。大多数货币是反向报价交易的。所以如果墨西哥比索从 17 走到 18，而你是做多比索的，那你就亏钱了，对吧？比索贬值了，等你把它换回来的时候，它能换到的美元更少了。我觉得这里面有一点，嗯，也许

turns.en: not misunderstanding, but there's plenty to scare investors off of the currency market. So the currency carry trade is one of the oldest strategies and institutional investing in plain English for the advisors watching this show. What does carry mean and why does it work as a
turns.zh: 算不上误解，但确实有太多东西能把投资者从货币市场上吓跑。那么，外汇套息交易（currency carry trade）是机构投资里最古老的策略之一。用大白话给正在看这档节目的顾问们讲讲：套息（carry）是什么意思，它为什么能作为一种

turns.en: return premium? Sure. Carry is just earning an interest rate period, right? So in a simple example, if I take Brazil, which is today yielding almost 12%, and I say, I want to be long Brazilian real, and I want to fund that with something that has a low yield, maybe Swiss franc, where the yield
turns.zh: 收益溢价存在？好。套息说白了就是赚一个利率差，对吧。举个简单的例子：如果我拿巴西来说，它今天的收益率接近 12%，我说我要做多巴西雷亚尔，然后我想用某个低收益率的东西来为它融资，比如瑞士法郎，它的收益率

turns.en: is slightly negative. The difference between those two, let's just say the 12% and call it minus one, which is not, but let's say it's minus one, that 13% is your carry. Period. That's what you should earn. Now, the reason it's scary is because sometimes that trade without warning, if you're not
turns.zh: 略微为负。两者之间的差额——就算一边是 12%，另一边姑且说是负 1%（其实不是，但我们假设是负 1%）——那 13% 就是你的套息收益，句号，这就是你本该赚到的。而它之所以吓人，是因为有时候这笔交易会在毫无预警的情况下，如果你没有

turns.en: watching the markets, can blow up in your face. That's the Achilles heel of most carry strategies, and that's what we are trying to solve for as we build Foxy in terms of how we select currencies, how we wait them, and how much risk we have in the fund.
turns.zh: 盯着市场，就会直接在你脸上炸开。这是大多数套息策略的阿喀琉斯之踵，也正是我们在构建 FOXY 时想要解决的问题——体现在我们如何挑选货币、如何给它们配权重，以及基金里承担多少风险。

turns.en: Yes, so you guys have, if I'm reading this correctly, two distinct strategies. The first is an emerging markets carry strategy. It's got eight currency pairs against US dollar. So can you walk us through how this piece works? Sure. So this is the primary carry engine of the
turns.zh: 是的，如果我没看错的话，你们有两套不同的策略。第一套是新兴市场套息策略，它有八个对美元的货币对。那你能给我们讲讲这一块是怎么运作的吗？好。这是整个策略最主要的套息引擎，

turns.en: strategy, primary return engine of the strategy, is to go long currencies where yields are high. So Brazil is kind of extreme. There are others that have lower amounts of yield in the domestic market, and against that, you are shorting currencies that have low yield. No emerging market currency
turns.zh: 也是策略最主要的收益引擎：做多那些收益率高的货币。巴西算是比较极端的例子，还有一些货币在本地市场上的收益率没那么高；与之相对，你做空的是那些低收益率的货币。没有任何一种新兴市场货币

turns.en: has a negative yield, but you're basically funding this high carry strategy with low carry currencies on the short side, and you pick up that difference. Now, I've characterized that as the return engine of the strategy, the G10 currencies, so dollar, euro, yen, Australia, dollar, and so on,
turns.zh: 的收益率是负的，但你实际上是在空头这一侧用低套息的货币为这个高套息策略融资，然后赚取中间那个差额。我把这一块描述成策略的收益引擎；而 G10 货币——也就是美元、欧元、日元、澳元等等——

turns.en: those currencies tend to be more as a cushion. They are prized for their ability to dampen volatility in the strategy, and the way that we use volatility itself as a signal is basically our guidepost for how much risk we want to take in the portfolio. When emerging market currencies
turns.zh: 这些货币更多是充当缓冲垫的角色。它们之所以被看重，是因为能压低策略里的波动率；而我们把波动率本身当作信号来用，这基本上就是我们决定组合中要承担多少风险的指路标。当新兴市场货币

turns.en: are signaling a lot of volatility coming in the future when implied volatility goes up, we're going to scale those back, and we will move more of the exposure into the G10 currencies, and that's our way to try and cushion or mitigate or guard, if you will, against that Achilles
turns.zh: 预示着未来会有大量波动时——也就是隐含波动率（implied volatility）上升时——我们就会把它们的仓位往回收，把更多的敞口挪到 G10 货币里去。这就是我们试图去缓冲、去减轻、或者说去防范那个阿喀琉斯

turns.en: heel of a traditional carry strategy. That was going to be my next question. That second part of the strategy, as you just mentioned, is the G10 currency mean reversion strategy. So what are you looking at there? Is it momentum, yield momentum? How does that mean reversion strategy work in the G10 space? You said it. It's yield momentum.
turns.zh: 之踵的办法——也就是传统套息策略的那个致命弱点。这本来是我的下一个问题。策略的第二部分，就像你刚提到的，是 G10 货币的均值回归（mean reversion）策略。那你在这块看的是什么？是动量、收益率动量吗？这个均值回归策略在 G10 这个领域里是怎么运作的？你自己说出来了，就是收益率动量（yield momentum）。

turns.en: Because developed economies have tended to be synchronized, they're not printing the same numbers in growth and inflation terms, but they've tended to move in the same direction going back 20 plus years. That tends to imply that monetary policy, which is the primary determinant of relative
turns.zh: 因为发达经济体往往是同步的：它们公布的增长和通胀数据并不相同，但往前推 20 多年，它们的走向大体是一致的。这往往意味着，货币政策——也就是决定 G10 内部相对

turns.en: exchange rate movements in G10 will also move in the same direction. So we use one signal, which is that implied yield, it's implied yield rather than yield momentum, but it's a yield momentum signal. We say, okay, if this currency is starting to run, we want if the implied yield
turns.zh: 汇率走势的首要因素——也会朝同一个方向移动。所以我们只用一个信号，也就是隐含收益率；准确说是隐含收益率，而不是收益率动量，但它本质上是一个收益率动量信号。我们会说，好，如果这个货币开始走强，如果隐含收益率

turns.en: momentum is going up, that's something we want to be long. And against that, because it will mean revert, if there are ones where implied yield momentum is low, we want to be short those. So again, two distinct signals for EM, it's just carry. We're ranking them, buying the high guys,
turns.zh: 动量在往上走，那就是我们想做多的对象。与之相对，因为它会均值回归，如果有些货币的隐含收益率动量很低，我们就想做空它们。所以还是两套不同的信号：对新兴市场来说，就是纯粹的套息，我们给它们排序，买入高的那些，

turns.en: shorting the low guys in G10, it's yield momentum. High yield momentum will buy those, be long, short the low or negative yield momentum. And then I saw like one of the key features of the fun that it's like, it's dollar neutral. Like so every long position has an equally sized short.
turns.zh: 做空低的那些；在 G10 里，则是收益率动量：收益率动量高的我们买入、做多，动量低的或者为负的我们就做空。然后我还看到这只基金的一个关键特征，就是它是美元中性（dollar neutral）的，也就是说每一个多头头寸都有一个同等规模的空头。

turns.en: So can you talk about why that construction matters and why Foxy, you know, it's not a bet on the direction necessarily of US dollar at all. 100%. There are great ETFs out there that will allow you to speculate on individual currencies. If you want euro, there's one for you. If you want broad,
turns.zh: 那你能讲讲为什么这种结构很重要，以及为什么 FOXY 根本不必然是在押注美元的方向吗？百分之百正确。市面上有很棒的 ETF，可以让你去投机单一货币。你想要欧元，有对应的产品；如果你觉得

turns.en: if you think the dollar is broadly weakening, there's an ETF for you. Foxy is different in terms of that dollar neutrality. And that to me is important. It's hard to make money betting on the direction of currencies. You have to have enough of those ideas and you have to be right often
turns.zh: 美元会全面走弱，也有对应的 ETF。FOXY 的不同之处就在于那种美元中性。这一点在我看来很重要。靠押注货币方向赚钱是很难的：你必须有足够多的这类判断，而且还得经常判断正确，

turns.en: enough for it to produce high absolute returns. That's really hard. If you're really good at it, you'll earn a nickname like George Soros broke the Bank of England back in 1992 because he bet against the British pound. He thought it was at an unsustainably strong level, put on a massive bet,
turns.zh: 足以带来很高的绝对收益。这真的很难。如果你真的特别擅长这件事，你就会赢得一个绰号——就像 George Soros 在 1992 年“击垮了英格兰银行”，因为他做空英镑。他认为英镑处在一个不可持续的强势水平上，于是下了一笔巨额赌注，

turns.en: the bank let the pound go while at the rest of history. That's hard to do. And I've done it for portions of my career. Do we like Colombian pesos, South African Rand? Do we not like Indonesian Rupiah? So Foxy avoids doing that. And all we're saying is we don't have a view on the direction of
turns.zh: 央行最终放弃了英镑，剩下的就是历史了。这种事很难做到。我职业生涯中有一部分时间确实在做这个：我们喜不喜欢哥伦比亚比索、南非兰特？我们是不是不喜欢印尼盾？FOXY 避免去做这种事。我们要说的只是：我们对
